verdicts.summary: Round 3, lens convex, full scope, read at commit f44cad4 on 2026-10-01. All 168 Specs read; the docs pages, component READMEs and helper sources were fetched today and are cited per finding. Not approved: 1 blocker, 6 majors, 15 minors. The five round-2 fixes: four confirmed (baseline batch bytes, paginator caps, backfill arithmetic, tenant argument on the pass-through), one partial (the restore stream check still leaves out the baseline event each rebuild reads). Leads: lead 3 holds as wording (components may declare typed environment variables; minor); lead 4 holds (a Node handler has no action that can run it; major); lead 5 holds as a design, with the take-effect behavior uncited and the switches untyped (minor). By rubric item. 22 holds: every write is in a mutation, the effect action writes nothing and each of its calls is its own transaction. 23 holds: component calls are `ctx.runMutation` or `ctx.runQuery`, the sub-transaction rule is stated, and the docs now also state that nested calls share the transaction limits, which the corpus still treats as unknown and does not use (`transactionLimits`, `ctx.meta.getTransactionMetrics()`; minor). 24 holds as a design rule; F11 and two Specs word it as a Convex prohibition (minor). 25 holds for the recorded exceptions (E-8, E-57); the eight obligation dispatch functions take no `tenantId` and that exemption is unrecorded (minor). 26 holds: index counts, field orders and nested paths match the queries, nothing orders on `_creationTime`; d02 states that Convex gives no global sequence, which the commit timestamp page contradicts (minor, owner question). 27 holds: indexed expected-version read, logical conflict told apart from engine retry, L1-11 encodes it; the bounded retry and its error are documented for caller-invoked mutations, while a scheduled mutation is retried without limit, which rebuild misstates (minor). 28 holds for stream and read-model budgets; the budgets are measured as JSON length and `budgetBytes` is not enforced at save (minor). 29 fails: receipts sweep, restore receipt check, generation purge, sweeper, retention and fan-out are bounded in documents only and cross 16 MiB at the corpus's own row ceilings (major); the restore stream check is at the ceiling once baselines are counted (minor); `rebuildSchedules` has one cursor for two scans (minor). 30 holds: scheduling commits with the mutation, at most 500 schedules in one mutation, actions never retried by Convex, authority on the record. 31 holds: lowercase `state.kind` literals, 7 day retention, no reliance on cancel stopping an action; the sweeper's reads of dispatch rows put it in conflict with the dispatches it watches (minor). 32 holds for what the backup page states; what a restore does to functions pending in the target and whether `--replace` equals a restore are stated as fact beyond the pages (minor); component coverage is correctly left to Probe 7. 33 holds: `ConvexError` data are validator values, a throw prevents the commit, F14 stays assumed with Probe 2. 34: F15 is marked assumed with Probe 5 as the rubric asks, and the using page now documents the reactivity half (minor). 35: the Workflow and Workpool facts match their READMEs; the migrations binding in rebuild cannot run as pinned and two statements about the component are stale (major). 36 holds: 1 second for queries and mutations, 30 and 10 minutes for actions, leases above both. Outside the numbered items: the first experiment's list query and the operator's needs-attention list declare return validators that reject the built-in `.paginate` result (blocker and major); the E-13 test identity passes Convex's visibility check for internal and component functions, so Sc L1-7's direct-call assertion cannot pass with it (major); and the generation row is both the batch checkpoint and a row every command reads, so each batch commit re-runs every command in flight during an online rebuild (major).
verdicts.reviewer: fable-xhigh agent, at the owner's instruction

ledger.issue: Three Specs disagree on how a UI double submit of a create is refused (Sc L1-4). outcome-boundary lists entityExists as a PlatformRejectionCode 'thrown by a context's identity check' (E-5), and idempotency-and-receipts says 'the context's identity index makes the second insert a rejection entityExists'. But outcome-model (E-21) reserves exactly two codes, staleVersion and operationTooLarge, and says 'every other code is the context's own'; initial-state says the creation command 'decides against initial() and typically rejects when the state says the subject already exists', i.e. a decider-owned code; and persistence-adapter's step1 to step10 contain no identity check that could raise entityExists. An implementer cannot tell whether the platform or the decider raises it, and the kernel's reserved list and the boundary's closed list conflict. The choice that the second submit is a rejection rather than an idempotent success is also a ruling the doc does not make and is not registered.
ledger.fix: Pick one owner and make the three families agree. Either (a) add a reserved third code to outcome-model E-21, add an adapter step between step2 and step4 that throws entityExists when a command declared as a create loads an existing stream, and cite it from outcome-boundary; or (b) drop entityExists from PlatformRejectionCode, make it a documented context code raised by decide against initial(), and reword idempotency-and-receipts line 92 and the ui-double-submit example accordingly. In both cases register 'second submit answers with a rejection, not an idempotent success' as an E-number with a [non-blocking] Extension question on idempotency-and-receipts.
ledger.note: One owner: entityExists is the kernel's third reserved code (outcome-model E-21), raised by the adapter's step 3 when a create planned at expectedVersion 0 loads an existing row (details.existing, details.current), before decide runs. initial-state's consequence, outcome-boundary's errorCodeEntityExists, idempotency's rule and uiDoubleSubmit bullet, and the L1-4 example now say the same. The 'second submit is a rejection, not an idempotent success' ruling is registered as E-39 with a [non-blocking] Extension question on idempotency-and-receipts and a README register row.

ledger.issue: do-nothing-check rules that 'a local reaction that needs none of the four may stay a plain scheduled mutation with a system-table scan, recorded as a per-reaction choice' and that 'every local reaction declares whether it is an obligation or a plain scheduled mutation'. The doc frames the do-nothing check as a check at activation of Layer 3, confirmed by Probe 7, not as a per-reaction opt-out that a developer decides; a per-reaction plain scheduled mutation escapes Law 8 (every installed durable capability ships recovery, inspection, retention) and Sc L3-7/L3-8 on the developer's judgment. The bullet cites (D13) with no [extension] marker, no E-number and no open question, and it contradicts d13's own alternative bullet, which says the do-nothing option is 'rejected for the durable profile'.
ledger.fix: Either remove the per-reaction opt-out and keep the ruling layer-wide (the obligation module is installed for the durable profile once Probe 7 shows the do-nothing option fails any Layer 3 scenario, which is what d13 already says), or keep it and mark both bullets [extension] with a new E-number (E-59 is free in the E range), add the matching [non-blocking] Extension question, list it in the README register, and state which laws a plain reaction must still satisfy (Law 7 by its own events, Law 8 by inheriting the module's inspect path) so the owner sees the bypass explicitly.
ledger.note: Took option (a): the per-reaction opt-out is removed. do-nothing-check's decision now says the check is made once for the durable profile and every local reaction of an installed durable profile is an obligation (Law 8); the consequence names the platform's own maintenance batches as the only plain scheduled mutations. d13 already said 'rejected for the durable profile' and needed no change.

ledger.issue: The doc's decision method rule 4 says Layers 0 to 2 get full detail, the first experiment runs, and Layer 3 is written from what it showed; the durable-layers preamble says 'the build that triggers a layer writes the rest'. The corpus writes Layer 3 now at 'Detail: full' with build-level numbers (cron every 60 s, grace 120 s, 5 rearms, backoff 1 s x2 capped 1 h, 8 attempts, 64 KiB payload, 16/500/8 fan-out bounds, 30-day horizon, ten indexes) under E-10, E-51, E-52, E-54, E-55, E-57, E-58, and every Layer 3 Spec states defined. The pre-emption is acknowledged only in README section 11 item 10 and PLAN.md section 11 item 10; no Layer 3 Spec carries it as an open question, so the graph does not show it and rubric item 5 ('Layer 3 has what D13 to D15 give') is not met for the numeric extensions. Not blocking, because README records it, but it is the one place where the corpus's detail stance departs from a doc rule without an in-graph record.
ledger.fix: Add to obligation-module and external-effects a '[non-blocking] Decision method rule 4: Layer 3 is written here before the first experiment; the numeric defaults in E-51, E-52, E-54, E-55, E-58 and the index set in E-57 are provisional until the experiment's measurements and Probe 7; the owner confirms that this does not pre-empt the experiment' (mirroring README item 10). Change the eight children's narrative line from 'Detail: full' to 'Detail: full where D13/D14/D15 rule; numbers provisional until the first experiment' and mark each numeric limit bullet as a provisional default. Alternatively downgrade the numeric bullets to [deferred] defaults and keep the structure; either way the deviation then lives in the graph, not only in README.
ledger.note: obligation-module and external-effects each carry a [non-blocking] 'Decision method rule 4' open question naming E-51/E-52/E-54/E-55/E-57/E-58 as provisional; the narrative line of obligation-module, external-effects and the nine children now reads 'full where D13/D14/D15 rule; numbers provisional until the first experiment'; the numeric limit bullets in wrapper, sweeper-adjacent, fan-out, record-contract, retention and claim-call-settle are marked provisional. README item 10 and the per-Spec question table updated.

ledger.issue: A duplicate is answered with duplicateResponse '{ kind: receipt.outcome, result: null, ..., replayed: true }' because receipts are thin (D6), but command-declaration says 'The declaration's output validator replaces result: v.any() in the entry's returns validator, so the wire type is closed per command', and command-pipeline's validatorCommandResponse says the same. A non-nullable output validator refuses null, so every replayed response of a receipted command fails its own returns validator and surfaces as a technical failure, which breaks Sc L1-3's 'one stored outcome' answer and Sc L1-8's disclosure test. The two extensions (E-30 wire shape, E-7/E-38 declaration) were written by the same package and never reconciled.
ledger.fix: Make the response shape honest to D6: declare CommandResponse⟨R⟩ as '{ ... result: R | null; replayed: boolean }' and build the entry's returns validator as v.union(decl.output, v.null()) for result (or make result optional and omit it on replay), state it in E-30's open question and in the command-declaration bullet, and have the retry-after-lost-response example assert result null against that validator.
ledger.note: Verified against docs.convex.dev/functions/validation: a value that does not match `returns` throws. Made the replay a first-class member of the closed wire type. command-pipeline.sdp.md: `CommandResponse⟨R⟩` is now `{ kind; operationId; affected; versions } & ({ replayed: false; result: R } | { replayed: true; result: null })`; `commandResponseValidator⟨R⟩(output)` is a `v.union` of the executed member (`result: output`, `replayed: v.literal(false)`) and the replayed member (`result: v.null()`, `replayed: v.literal(true)`); both entries declare `returns: commandResponseValidator(placeOrderDeclaration.output)`; E-30's open question, step 5 and a new Verification bullet state it. command-declaration.sdp.md Contract now says the `output` validator is the executed member's `result` and `result` is null exactly when `replayed` is true. idempotency-and-receipts.sdp.md `duplicateResponse` names the replayed member and the `v.null()` branch.

ledger.issue: E-7 binds every command to two registered functions (publicCommand and internalCommand). The doc counts registered functions as a standing cost (decision method rule 2) and D7 rejects a per-command body precisely because it 'doubles the functions every command needs'. command-declaration's risk bullet mentions only hand-written export lines; d12's consequence says the standing cost is 'one declaration per command'; the E-7 open question does not record the doubled function count nor the cheaper alternative the doc's own D7 suggests (one public export per command plus one generic internal dispatcher keyed by commandType from the static registry, at the price of losing tsc-typed internal callers for Sc L2-4). Rule 5 asks each mechanism to be refuted against a cheaper design.
ledger.fix: In command-declaration's E-7 open question and risk, state the standing cost (two registered mutations per command) and name the rejected alternative (single public export plus a generic internal dispatcher, as D7's dispatcher already does) with the reason it lost (typed internal callers and the registration check of Sc L2-4). Add the same cost line to d12's consequence so the decision Spec's cost accounting matches the design.
ledger.note: command-declaration gained a risk bullet (two registered mutations per command) and its E-7 question now names the refuted alternative (one public export plus a generic internal dispatcher keyed by commandType from the registry) and why it lost (untyped internal callers defeat Sc L2-4's tsc check; string lookup of the contract version). d12's cost consequence records the doubled function count and cites E-7.

ledger.issue: Three rules go a step beyond their citation without an [extension] marker. journal.sdp.md line 48 adds by_operation as a fourth starting index, calling it 'the operation index the doc implies' and citing (D2, D19), while the doc says to start with three and add others 'when a real query needs them' (tables.sdp.md does register it under E-3, journal does not). decider-contract.sdp.md line 39 rules that parent-captured facts are excluded from the receipt fingerprint and that 'a retry that captures a fresher fact is not a conflict', cited (D3, D6), while D6 defines the fingerprint only as business input plus contract version and idempotency-and-receipts' fingerprintInputs never mentions facts. write-pause.sdp.md line 47 makes every gate change a fail-closed audit record, cited (D19), while D19 fails closed only for 'mandatory business or security audit'; whether gate changes are mandatory audit is the design's call.
ledger.fix: journal line 48: mark [extension] under E-3 and name the real query (restore's receipt check and diagnosis by operation ID) as the reason it starts now. decider-contract line 39: mark [extension] under E-36 and add 'captured facts' to idempotency-and-receipts' fingerprintInputs exclusion list so both Specs say the same thing. write-pause line 47: mark [extension] under E-8 ('gate changes are treated as mandatory audit').
ledger.note: journal: by_operation is now a separate [extension] rule under E-3 naming the two real queries (restore's receipt check, diagnosis by operation ID). decider-contract line 39 is [extension] under E-36 and idempotency's fingerprintInputs and E-36 question exclude captured facts. write-pause's audit bullet is [extension] under E-8 ('gate changes treated as mandatory audit').

ledger.issue: The vocabulary defines caller namespace as 'such as public, worker, agent or system', while actor-and-scope pins the closed union public, service, worker, agent, system (E-6) and the receipts example space uses 'service'. The model Spec every pack refs should list the closed set or say it is open-ended by design.
ledger.fix: Change the vocabulary entry to name the five values of E-6 exactly, or drop the list and point at actor-and-scope as the one closed union.
ledger.note: The vocabulary entry names the closed union public, service, worker, agent, system and points at actor-and-scope's E-6.

ledger.issue: rebuild states as an assumption that @convex-dev/migrations 'defaults to batches of 100' and its limitBatchSize bullet calls 100 'the migrations component's default'. PLAN.md section 9 records that batch size configuration is not on the product page and instructs Package D to state the batch bound as a design choice under F13; the corpus cites no README read for the number. A fact presented as the component's default without a source is the v0.1 order the decision method reverses.
ledger.fix: Either cite the migrations README with its read date (as Package E does for S11/S12) in measurableBy of F17 and in the rebuild bullet, or reword both bullets to '100 entities, a design choice under E-40 and F13 until Probe 6', dropping 'the component's default'.
ledger.note: Took the reword option and also sourced the number: read the @convex-dev/migrations README on 2026-09-30 (it states 'The component will fetch your data in batches of 100', a configurable batchSize, customRange, and continuation from the failed batch). rebuild.sdp.md's assumption now cites the README with its read date and separates what it does not say (iterating a table inside a component, Probe 6); limitBatchSize now reads '100 entities ... by default, a design choice under E-40 and F13 until Probe 6, and the number the migrations README, read 2026-09-30, states as the component's default'. F17's measurableBy (specs/facts, Package A) is untouched; it could add the same README citation.

ledger.issue: E-44's BusinessFailurePolicy 'reject' lets a use case turn a context's committed business failure into a rejection so nothing commits. D4 says a business failure 'belongs in history' and 'commits like a success', and that whether a refused request becomes a fact is chosen per command. Since D10 makes the use case the command, the ruling is defensible, but the E-44 open question does not say that 'reject' un-commits what the context judged to belong in history, so the owner cannot see the D4 tension when confirming the extension.
ledger.fix: Extend the E-44 open question with one sentence: 'reject rolls back events the context recorded as a business failure; the doc's per-command choice is read as the use case's, since D10 makes the use case the command; the owner confirms that a context's business failure may be overridden by its caller.'
ledger.note: parent-use-cases.sdp.md E-44 open question now states that reject rolls back the events the context recorded as its business failure, which D4 says belong in history, that the doc's per-command choice is read as the use case's because D10 makes the use case the command, and that the owner confirms a context's business failure may be overridden by its caller (E-44, D4, D10).

ledger.issue: The context queries contract pins `list` (queries.sdp.md:57) and `history` (:58) as component queries that call `.paginate(paginationOpts)`, `paginationShape` (:61) says the result is what `.paginate` returns, and `parentPassThrough` (:62) relays it to the client; `fnDefineStreamQueries` (:55) types both as `PaginationResult`. The rebuild's `fnEnumerateCall` (rebuild.sdp.md:97), `backfillBatch` step3 and the restore's `streamCheckBatch`/`receiptCheckBatch` (restore.sdp.md:87, :89) all enumerate through that `list` page. Convex documents that the built-in `.paginate()` does not work inside a component, so as written the Layer 1 list/history queries and the Layer 2 backfill, verify and restore enumeration are unimplementable with the pinned API. Probe 5 records only reactivity and how a cursor crosses the boundary as open; it does not record that the mechanism itself is documented as unsupported.
ledger.fix: In `defineStreamQueries`, implement `list` and `history` with `paginator(ctx.db, schema).query("streams"|"events").withIndex(...).paginate(paginationOpts)` from `convex-helpers/server/pagination`; keep `paginationOptsValidator` in `args` and the `{ page, isDone, continueCursor }` result, so `fnEnumerateCall`, the rebuild batches and the restore batches need no change. Rewrite `paginationShape` and `parentPassThrough` to say the parent relays the helper's page and that a reactive client uses `usePaginatedQuery` from `convex-helpers/react` (the built-in hook cannot maintain the journal across the boundary). Record the documented fact on F15 or a new fact Spec with S4 as its source, narrow Probe 5 to reactivity plus the helper's end-cursor behaviour, and add `convex-helpers` to the context component's standing cost (E-22/E-24).
ledger.note: Verified against docs.convex.dev/components/authoring and the convex-helpers README. queries: list and history use paginator(ctx.db, schema)...paginate(paginationOpts) from convex-helpers/server/pagination, keep paginationOptsValidator and the {page,isDone,continueCursor} result, so rebuild's fnEnumerateCall and restore's batches keep their shape; paginationShape and parentPassThrough say the parent relays the helper's page and the client uses usePaginatedQuery from convex-helpers/react; new componentPagination bullet. read-models' pagination bullet, rebuild's enumeration paragraph, F15's narrative and measurableBy, probe-plan's Probe 5 question and flow are narrowed to reactivity plus end-cursor contiguity. convex-helpers added to the context component's standing cost (E-22) and a dependencyConvexHelpers bullet.

ledger.issue: `fnWriteBaseline` (journal.sdp.md:83) declares `writeBaseline` with the component's `internalMutation` builder, yet `convexSurface` (context-component.sdp.md:98) lists `maintenance.writeBaseline` as part of the component API the parent calls, and the flow (journal.sdp.md:64) plus `limitBaselineBatch` (:84) have a migration loop drive it in batches "with `@convex-dev/migrations` or a scheduled mutation chain". A component's internal functions are not exposed to the parent, so the parent cannot call it; and `@convex-dev/migrations` cannot iterate the context's `streams` table anyway. Separately, the pinned args (`tenantId, streamType, streamIds, migrationName, actor, operation`) carry neither the migrated state nor a migration function reference, while `baselineRow` (:82) says the call writes "the migrated state" and the flow says the migration folds with the old reducer, which the corpus also says is not kept. An implementer cannot tell who computes the migrated state or where the driver runs.
ledger.fix: Declare `writeBaseline` with the component's `mutation` builder (its public visibility becomes an internal reference to the parent and stays unreachable by clients), or keep it `internalMutation` and state that the driver is a self-scheduled internal mutation chain inside the component. In either case replace the `@convex-dev/migrations` mention with the parent-side (or component-side) scheduled chain that pages the context's enumeration, and add to the args either `migration: { key, version }` resolved from a static migration registry inside the component (which holds the old reducer for that one migration) or the per-stream migrated states computed by the driver. Bound the batch by events folded, not only by streams, since a fold per stream reads its tail since the last baseline.
ledger.note: Verified against docs.convex.dev/components/authoring ("Only public functions are accessible: Internal functions are not exposed to the parent app"). journal.sdp.md: `fnWriteBaseline` is now `mutation` from the component's own builder, built by a new `defineMaintenance(journal, registrations)`; args are `{ tenantId, streamType, migrationName, actor, operationId, correlationId?, afterStreamId?, maxStreams? }` returning `{ written, skipped, eventsRead, nextAfterStreamId }`. The migrated state now has a source: `StreamRegistration` gains `stateSchemaVersion` and `baselineMigrations: readonly BaselineMigration⟨S⟩[]`, a static registry inside the component, and `BaselineMigration = { name, fromSchemaVersion, toSchemaVersion, readsHistory, migrate: (saved, history) => S }` (`migratedStateSource` bullet: the saved state is the old reducer's fold, so no old reducer is kept; events are read only when `readsHistory`). The `@convex-dev/migrations` mention is gone (`driverNotMigrationsComponent`); the driver is a parent-side scheduled internal mutation chain paging the context's `by_identity` enumeration by `afterStreamId` (`baselineDriver`, `driverTenancy`, `writeBaselineIdempotence`), citing F2/F8/F9. `limitBaselineBatch` bounds 100 streams and, when history is read, 4,000 events per call. Frontmatter: F17 dropped (no longer cited), F8, F9, Law 6, Law 11 added. Two flows rewritten. Out of scope and left for the README owner (Package A): README.md's E-25 register row still calls `writeBaseline` an "internal mutation".

ledger.issue: Bounds are stated in documents while the binding ceiling is bytes, at the corpus's own 256 KiB stream-document budget (state-document-mapping.sdp.md:52). `limitListPage` (queries.sdp.md:66) says 200 rows "stays far under the 16 MiB read ceiling at the stream document budget": 200 x 256 KiB = 50 MiB. `limitBatchSize` (rebuild.sdp.md:114) reads 100 stream rows through `list` in one mutation: 25 MiB. `limitReadsPerCall` (context-component.sdp.md:110) allows 256 streams per operation call: 64 MiB, plus up to 32 parts each under the derived mapping (state-document-mapping.sdp.md:53 already concedes 8 MiB for one stream). `limitCheckBatch` (restore.sdp.md:93) makes 25 `rebuild` calls in one mutation while `limitFoldPerStream` (:94) budgets each fold at 1,000 events x 16 KiB = 16 MiB, i.e. up to 400 MiB in one transaction. The corpus itself rules (batch-shaped-api.sdp.md:21) that every bound assumes limits add up across nested calls until Probe 4 answers, and a nested `runQuery` runs in the calling mutation's transaction, so these bounds are not below the ceiling and rubric item 29 fails.
ledger.fix: Derive every enumeration and call bound from bytes: with a 256 KiB stream budget, 16 MiB admits at most 64 full rows, so cap `numItems` for `list` and the backfill/verify batch at 32 (or lower the stream budget and say so), set the default `maxStreams` so that streams x budget stays under 8 MiB (32 at 256 KiB) and let an operation raise it only with a smaller declared state budget; add a metadata-only `enumerate` query returning `{ streamId, streamVersion, deletedAt }` for verify and restore so they never read state; make the restore stream check one fold per mutation or bound the batch by cumulative `eventsApplied` (e.g. stop when the running sum passes 500 events); restate `limitListPage`, `limitBatchSize`, `limitReadsPerCall` and `limitCheckBatch` as byte bounds and have the first experiment report bytes read per call alongside documents.
ledger.note: Bounds are now derived from bytes: StateDocumentMapping gains budgetBytes (default 256 KiB, E-2) and a budgetDerivedBounds bullet; the adapter's step 1 and limitStreamsPerCall cap the planned streams' budgets at 8 MiB (32 streams at the default, 256 for a small stream type); limitDocumentsWrittenPerCall is 800 documents and 8 MiB; list's numItems is min(200, floor(8 MiB / budgetBytes)) and rebuild's batch is capped by it; restore's stream check stops after the fold that passes 500 cumulative eventsApplied and 25 streams, citing S3 (runQuery runs in the caller's transaction) and Probe 4; the first experiment reports bytes read per call. Rejected the metadata-only enumerate suggestion: Convex counts the full documents a query reads, so a projection of fields does not reduce data read per transaction.

ledger.issue: `typeObligationView` (operator-operations.sdp.md:52) types `dispatch.state` as the string literals `"Pending" | "InProgress" | "Success" | "Failed" | "Canceled"`, and the sweeper contract (sweeper.sdp.md:41-43) and PLAN.md:620/:653 use the same capitalized names. The system document's `state` field is an object whose `kind` is a lowercase literal, and the failed variant carries the error; an implementer mapping `row.state.kind` will not find the pinned literals.
ledger.fix: Type the view from the system row: `dispatch: { state: "pending" | "inProgress" | "success" | "failed" | "canceled" | "missing"; error?: string; scheduledTime?: number; completedTime?: number }` read from `row.state.kind` (and `row.state.error` when failed), and let the sweeper's `lastError` of class `wrapper` take that error string; keep the docs' capitalized names only in prose.
ledger.note: Verified on the scheduling page (state: { kind: 'success' }). operator-operations' typeObligationView types dispatch.state from the lowercase state.kind with error from state.error and 'missing' for a null row; sweeper gained a dispatchStateRead bullet, step2 compares row.state.kind, recoverOne takes dispatchError and records lastError of class wrapper/dispatchFailed on the rearmed record. Contract prose keeps the docs' capitalized names. PLAN.md left untouched: it is orchestrator-owned and its mentions are prose.

ledger.issue: E-12 (events-stay-small.sdp.md:31, target `event.payload.bytes.lte:16384`) justifies 16 KiB by "a fold of 1,000 events stays under the 16 MiB read ceiling with room for the envelope": 1,000 x 16,384 B = 15.6 MiB leaves about 393 bytes per event for an envelope that holds two UUIDs, an actor object and eight further fields, plus the stream row, so the headroom is nil. `limitRebuildRead` (journal.sdp.md:85, queries.sdp.md:68) and `limitFoldPerStream` (restore.sdp.md:94) repeat the 1,000-event figure. None of them mentions that a `rebuild` query must also fold and deep-compare 16 MiB inside the 1-second query execution limit, which binds first.
ledger.fix: State the fold budget with headroom (e.g. 12 KiB payloads or 600 events since the latest baseline), count the envelope in `limitRebuildRead`, and record that the 1-second query timeout, not the read ceiling, is the binding limit for a fold, to be measured by the first experiment and the L2-7 example.
ledger.note: Fold bound is 600 events since the latest baseline (about 10 MiB with a 1 KiB envelope, headroom under 16 MiB) as journal's limitFoldEvents; events-stay-small's narrative, E-12 question, risk and measurableBy, queries' limitRebuildRead and limitHistoryPage, and restore's limitFoldPerStream restated; each records that the 1-second query timeout binds first and the first experiment and L2-7 measure it. README E-12 row updated.

ledger.issue: For the same bound of 1,000 affected refs and 1,000 stream versions, `limitRowSize` (receipt-table.sdp.md:57) says a row stays under 400 KiB while `limitAffectedRefs` (idempotency-and-receipts.sdp.md:95) says under 200 KiB.
ledger.fix: Use one figure in both Specs (about 400 KiB at 200 bytes per entry) or lower the ref bound to 500 and keep 200 KiB.
ledger.note: Kept the figure whose arithmetic is shown: receipt-table.sdp.md `limitRowSize` says 2,000 entries under 200 bytes each keep a row under 400 KiB (1 MiB document limit confirmed on docs.convex.dev/production/state/limits) and declares itself the corpus's one figure. idempotency-and-receipts.sdp.md `limitAffectedRefs` keeps the 1,000/1,000 bound and cites `limitRowSize` instead of restating a size.

ledger.issue: `limitSweepBatch` (sweeper.sdp.md:63) bounds one run at 100 candidates plus 100 expired leases by documents read and written, but each candidate costs a `ctx.db.system.get`, a nested `ctx.runMutation(internal.obligations.recoverOne)` and a schedule (steps 1-5, :57-61); with F4's per-call overhead unmeasured, 200 nested mutations in one 1-second mutation is the binding constraint, not the document count.
ledger.fix: Mark the 100-candidate bound as provisional on Probe 3, add an elapsed-time guard to the loop (stop after about 500 ms and leave the rest for the next cron tick, counting the remainder as a metric), or lower the per-run bound to 25 until measured.
ledger.note: Applied the first two of the three proposed fixes together in design/specs/obligations/sweeper.sdp.md: the 100-candidate bound is now marked provisional on Probe 3 (new `[non-blocking] Probe 3 pending` open question, F4 added to constrainedBy and Traces, `limitSweepBatch` rewritten to say the 200 nested calls are the binding cost), and the loop has an elapsed-time guard `limitSweepElapsed` of 500 ms checked before each candidate and each lease, with the remainder counted as a new `deferred` field in `sweep`'s return and fed into the health metric. Verified against Convex docs (docs.convex.dev/functions/runtimes, read 2026-09-30): `Date.now()` is frozen for the whole function execution, so the guard reads `performance.now()`, which the page says increments inside mutations; the narrative records that recheck. Did not lower the bound to 25: the guard makes the run safe whatever Probe 3 measures, and `boundTest` says the bound is lowered to what the guard admits at the bound test.

ledger.issue: Three Specs give three different answers to who writes a read model and with what signature. command-pipeline Step 9 says "the executor runs the projection of every read model the declaration lists" and its `readModelWrites` bullet says the pipeline updates them "after step 8 returns"; command-declaration pins `ReadModelBinding.update(ctx, { tenantId, operationId, result: unknown, versions })` and says read models are "updated at the pipeline's step 9"; parent-use-cases' flow says "The body updates every read model it declares with the projection contract" and its `createdDetection` bullet needs the per-stream created flag from the context DTO to pick the `live-created` mode; projection-contract's only writer is `applyProjection(ctx, projection, { tenantId, dto, versions, mode, generations })`. `ReadModelBinding.update` receives the use case's `result: unknown`, not the DTOs and not the mode or generations, so it cannot call `applyProjection` as pinned. An implementer cannot tell whether the pipeline or the executor body writes, nor which signature to implement (rubric item 17: step sequences must agree).
ledger.fix: Pick one owner and one signature. Recommended: the executor body calls `applyProjection`/`applyAggregate` per declared read model (it alone holds the DTOs, the created flag and the mode), pipeline Step 9 becomes "the executor has written every read model the declaration lists through `applyProjection`; the pipeline writes none itself", and `ReadModelBinding` is redefined as `{ name: string; version: number; projection: Projection⟨D, Row⟩ }` used by the registry check and `scopesOfUseCase`, with no `update` member. Update command-declaration's Contract bullet and the L1-2 `failure-before-receipt` example wording accordingly.
ledger.note: Picked the pipeline as the one owner (two of the three findings on this topic point there and it keeps the declaration's readModels list as the wiring fact): step 9 reads generationsToWrite per binding and calls applyProjection/applyAggregate per matching streams entry, mode from the entry's created flag; ReadModelBinding is { name, version, source: { contextId, streamType }, projection } with no update member; the executor returns ExecutorResult = CommittedOutcome plus streams. command-declaration's Contract, parent-use-cases' rule, flows, typeExecutor and createdDetection, projection-contract's callers bullet and verification, and read-models' write-path paragraph all say this. The L1-2 failure-before-receipt example already reads correctly (read models written before the receipt insert).

ledger.issue: A duplicate is answered with `result: null` (idempotency `duplicateResponse`, `tombstoneResponse`; the retry-after-lost-response example asserts `result` null), but the pipeline pins `CommandResponse⟨R⟩.result: R` and command-declaration says the declaration's `output` validator replaces `result: v.any()` in the entry's `returns` validator so the wire type is closed per command. A replayed response then fails the mutation's `returns` validator at runtime for any command whose output validator does not accept null, which is every command. The two Specs contradict each other on the response shape.
ledger.fix: Make the replayed case part of the closed type: `type CommandResponse⟨R⟩ = { ...; result: R | null; replayed: boolean }` with `result: v.union(decl.output, v.null())` in the composed `returns`, and state in command-declaration that `result` is null exactly when `replayed` is true. Add one `rule:` line in idempotency-and-receipts saying the returns validator admits null for a replay.
ledger.note: Same root fix as the fidelity finding. Added the requested `rule:` in idempotency-and-receipts.sdp.md: a replay answers with `result` null and the entry's returns validator admits it on its replayed member, so a duplicate is a value under the closed wire type and never a validator failure (D6, E-30). command-declaration.sdp.md states `result` is null exactly when `replayed` is true. The retry-after-lost-response example's Verification bullet now asserts the response arrived as a return value under that validator.

ledger.issue: The decider contract says the decision context carries "the outside facts the parent captured" (`DecisionContext.facts`), the adapter reads them from `ExecuteRequest.facts` and declares `OperationArgs⟨I⟩ = { tenantId; actor; operation; input; facts? }`, but the registered operation's validators are fixed as `argsCommon: { tenantId, actor, operation, input }` with no `facts` field, the pipeline's `contextCall` passes `{ tenantId, actor, operation, input }`, and the `Executor⟨I, R⟩` call shape has no facts at all. Convex argument validators refuse an unknown field, so a parent that passes `facts` fails validation and one that does not leaves `request.facts` undefined. The kernel's purity rule depends on facts entering as inputs, and there is no input.
ledger.fix: Either add `facts: v.optional(v.record(v.string(), v.any()))` to `argsCommon` in context-component, to the pipeline's `contextCall` and to the `Executor` call (`{ tenantId, actor, operation, input, facts }`), and say where the parent captures them (step 7 or the executor); or remove `facts` from `OperationArgs`/`ExecuteRequest`/`DecisionContext` and state that captured facts travel inside `input` and are excluded from the fingerprint by the declaration. State the choice once and cite it from the other three Specs.
ledger.note: argsCommon gains facts: v.optional(v.record(v.string(), v.any())); the pipeline's contextCall and step 8 pass facts; runOperation defaults facts to {}; the executor captures them (factsCapture bullets in the pipeline and parent-use-cases) so the Executor call itself carries no facts field, which is the one deviation from the finding's first option: the executor is the producer, not a consumer, of facts. The fingerprint exclusion is stated in both decider-contract (E-36 marker) and idempotency.

ledger.issue: outcome-boundary lists `entityExists` in the closed `PlatformRejectionCode` union and says it is "thrown by a context's identity check when a create command's client-generated entity ID already exists"; idempotency-and-receipts says "the context's identity index makes the second insert a rejection `entityExists`". But the kernel outcome model reserves only two codes for the adapter (`staleVersion`, `operationTooLarge`; README says the same), the adapter's ten steps contain no identity check (step 2 loads the existing row, step 9 patches it), and initial-state's consequence says the creation command is refused by the decider ("typically rejects when the state says the subject already exists"), which would be a context-owned code, not a platform one. Sc L1-4 binds `second: "entity exists"`, so the scenario depends on a code nobody produces.
ledger.fix: Choose one producer. Either reserve `entityExists` in the kernel (add `rejectionCodeEntityExists` beside the other two, add an adapter step between 2 and 3: "when the operation declares `creates: true` and `loaded.exists`, throw `entityExists` with `details.existing`", and add `creates` to `OperationDeclaration`), or drop it from `PlatformRejectionCode` and make it a domain code the Orders decider declares in `rejections`. Align initial-state, idempotency `uiDoubleSubmit`, the L1-4 example and the README's "two reserved codes" sentence with the choice.
ledger.note: Producer is the adapter's step 3 on expectedVersion === 0 && loaded.exists; a new adapter Contract bullet, errorCodeEntityExists in the adapter and the boundary, initial-state's createExpectsVersionZero, and uniqueValueWorked (claim streams planned at version 0) agree. README's Layer 0 paragraph and E-21 row say three reserved codes. No new adapter step or creates flag was needed: the plan's expected version is the existing mechanism.

ledger.issue: rebuild's write-pause flow says "the operator closes the maintenance gate for the read model's scope before `startGeneration`", but the gate can only let a background writer through by its generation: write-pause `closeGate` takes an optional `generationId`, `assertWritable(ctx, scopes, allowGeneration)` throws unless "the closed entry's `generationId` equals `allowGeneration`", and rebuild step2 returns without writing "when a closed scope covers this read model and the gate was not closed for this generation". A gate closed before the generation row exists cannot name it, so the paused backfill's own batches refuse themselves and the L2-6 examples cannot reach `verified`.
ledger.fix: Reverse or fuse the order: `startGeneration` with `pauseRequired: true` inserts the generation row and calls the close in the same mutation (or patches the already-closed scope's `generationId` to the new row), and the rebuild flow reads "startGeneration closes the gate for the read model's scope and records its own generation on the closed entry". Update the write-pause Contract bullet and the L2-6 examples' first verification bullet to match.
ledger.note: Fused the order: startGeneration with pauseRequired inserts the generation row and calls a new write-pause helper closeScope for the read-model scope with the new row's ID, before scheduling the first batch, all in one mutation (rebuild flow, fnStartGeneration). write-pause gains fnCloseScope and fnResumeScope helpers; closeGate no longer takes a generationId and is the operator's entry for a tenant or the all scope only; the Contract bullet says the closed entry always names a row that exists; abortGeneration calls resumeScope. Both L2-6 examples' first verification bullet now starts the generation and asserts the gate is closed with this generation on the closed entry. Added a reviewer bullet that only startGeneration closes a read-model scope for a rebuild.

ledger.issue: Two Specs combine into mass escalation during any maintenance window. The wrapper treats every transient `ConvexError` as a retryable attempt: it "increments the attempt count" and reschedules with backoff 1 s × 2 capped at 1 h, 8 attempts by default, so the whole budget is spent in about two minutes. The write pause and `MAINTENANCE_MODE=restore` refuse every use case in scope with the transient `writePaused`, and fan-out-and-chains routes every derived command through the pipeline, hence through `assertWritable`. A cross-stream rebuild or a restore drill that lasts longer than two minutes therefore moves every local reaction in scope to `needsAttention` with reason `exhausted`, contradicting D13's rule that "a full worker pool delays work and never turns valid intent into a rejection" and Sc L3-3. Separately, application/restore sequences only `MAINTENANCE_MODE` and retention-and-restore sequences only `OBLIGATIONS_DISPATCH`; neither says whether `rebuildSchedules` (which rearms local wrappers) runs before or after `MAINTENANCE_MODE` clears, and the README lists the two switches only as a simplification question.
ledger.fix: In local-reaction-wrapper add a step before step8: a transient `writePaused` or `capacity` refusal is a delay, not an attempt: reschedule the same attempt ID after the gate's drain interval (or `retryAfterMs`) without incrementing `attemptCount`, and cite D13's full-pool rule. In retention-and-restore state the order: `rebuildSchedules` and the reconcile pass run only after application/restore has cleared `MAINTENANCE_MODE`, and application/restore's accepted branch names that hand-off. Cross-cite the two restore workflows from each other.
ledger.note: Wrapper: new Contract bullet and step8 defer an attempt refused with transient writePaused or capacity at retryAfterMs or limitDeferralDelay (60 s) without touching attemptNumber, activeAttemptId or attemptCount; old steps renumbered 9 and 10; errorClassification updated. lifecycle-transitions gained the [extension] maintenance-deferral pending-to-pending rule under E-51. fan-out-and-chains says a derived command meets the gate and is deferred. Restore order: application/restore's accepted branch clears MAINTENANCE_MODE then hands off; retention-and-restore's restoreStep1-3 run rebuildSchedules only after that, rebuildSchedules refuses while MAINTENANCE_MODE=restore, OBLIGATIONS_DISPATCH moves last; both workflows cross-cite; README residual item updated.

ledger.issue: `fnWriteBaseline` is declared with the component's `internalMutation` builder in the component's `maintenance` module, and the journal flow has "a migration ... calls `writeBaseline` per stream in bounded batches ... with `@convex-dev/migrations` or a scheduled mutation chain", i.e. a caller in the parent. The Convex components authoring page (S4) states that only a component's public functions are exposed to the parent app and internal functions are not; the corpus's own `clientReach` bullet already relies on the same rule (public component functions become internal references). As written the baseline migration, and therefore Sc L2-7, cannot be driven from the parent.
ledger.fix: Declare `writeBaseline` with the component's `mutation` builder (it is still unreachable by clients per S4) and say so in a `componentBuilders`-style bullet; or state that the baseline migration is defined inside the component and the parent only triggers it. Apply the same check to any other component function the parent must call.
ledger.note: Same journal edits as the previous finding, plus context-component.sdp.md: `componentBuilders` now names only `mutation` and `query` and states that every function the parent calls (operations, queries, `maintenance.writeBaseline`) uses the public builders because internal functions are not exposed to the parent; new `parentReach` Design bullet (S4). Checked every other parent-called function in the package: operations (`defineOperation`) and the five queries were already public builders, so nothing else changed. The L2-7 example's executable verification now says the parent test mutation calls `maintenance.writeBaseline` through `ctx.runMutation` with a registered migration name and expects `written` 1 and `nextAfterStreamId` null.

ledger.issue: journal's flow says "Before writing, the adapter reads the events index for any version above the expected one; a hit for a caller-named version is the `staleVersion` rejection", while the adapter answers the caller-named case at step 3 by comparing `target.expectedVersion` with the loaded stream row and treats any index hit at step 8 as a defect ("the caller-named case was answered in step 3 and a hit here means the row and the index disagree").
